articles.title: I built a bank statement to Excel converter that never uploads your PDF
articles.excerpt: Most "PDF bank statement to Excel" sites want you to upload the file. Think about what's on that PDF: your name, your address, your account number, and every payment you made last month. I wouldn't ha…
articles.body: Most "PDF bank statement to Excel" sites want you to upload the file. Think about what's on that PDF: your name, your address, your account number, and every payment you made last month. I wouldn't hand that to a site I'd never heard of, so when I built one for my own site I set one rule before writing any code. The file never leaves the browser tab. This is how it works, including the parts that are still fragile. It's plain JavaScript, one ES module of about 230 lines plus Mozilla's pdf.js, with no backend at all. If you'd rather try it before reading, it's live as a free bank statement to Excel converter on my studio's site. Reading text out of a PDF A PDF doesn't contain lines or tables.

articles.title: Are Passkeys a Trap? How to Back Them Up So a Lost Phone Can't Lock You Out
articles.excerpt: The usual argument that passkeys are a trap goes like this: Apple, Google and Microsoft want your logins stuck in their ecosystems. In October 2026 that argument is a year out of date. You can now mov…
articles.body: The usual argument that passkeys are a trap goes like this: Apple, Google and Microsoft want your logins stuck in their ecosystems. In October 2026 that argument is a year out of date. You can now move passkeys out of Apple Passwords and Google Password Manager into a third-party manager with an official, encrypted transfer. The thing that will actually lock you out of your accounts is much less interesting. You have one phone, every passkey lives on it, and it ends up at the bottom of a lake. Further down is how I back them up so that can't happen: one synced manager you picked yourself, plus two hardware keys. Scott Helme published Passkeys are not a trap this week as a reply to a viral "Passkeys are a trap. Do not use them" post, and the Hacker News thread turned into the usual brawl.

articles.title: Firefox Tab Management: From Tab Groups to Session Saver — Taming 100+ Tabs
articles.excerpt: Tab hoarding is real. Studies suggest most power users have 20–200+ tabs open at once. Firefox has more tab management tools than most people know about, and extensions like Tab Manager & Session Save…
articles.body: Tab hoarding is real. Studies suggest most power users have 20–200+ tabs open at once. Firefox has more tab management tools than most people know about, and extensions like Tab Manager & Session Saver solve the deeper problem: saving and restoring named sessions of related tabs. The Tab Overload Problem Tabs serve different purposes: Reference — documentation, specs, articles you haven't read yet Work in progress — the 6 tabs for the feature you're building "I'll read this later" — articles bookmarked via tabs Background — email, Slack, calendar Research — 15 tabs for a decision you're making Having all of these in one browser window creates cognitive overhead. Context switching between "work" and "research" tabs means scrolling through everything.

articles.body: Night mode for the web is inconsistent — some sites respect your OS dark mode preference, others have their own dark mode settings, and some don't support dark mode at all. NightOwl is a Firefox extension that applies dark mode universally across all websites, using intelligent color inversion that preserves images and media. The Problem with Dark Mode on the Web OS-level dark mode ( prefers-color-scheme: dark ) only works if the website implements CSS dark mode: /* Site developer wrote this */ @media ( prefers-color-scheme : dark ) { body { background : #111 ; color : #eee ; } } Most modern sites do implement this. But many older sites, documentation pages, and blogs don't — they're always white backgrounds.

articles.excerpt: CD Projekt Red has finally spoken up about the live-action Cyberpunk 2077 movie. The company said it doesn’t want to do a 1:1 adaptation of the game, instead telling a new story within the same univer…
articles.body: CD Projekt Red has finally spoken up about the live-action Cyberpunk 2077 movie . The company said it doesn’t want to do a 1:1 adaptation of the game, instead telling a new story within the same universe. "At this point, we can only say that we definitely don't want to make a film adaptation of the game," co-CEO Michał Nowakowski told Polish outlet PAP Biznes , via GamesRadar . "We want to tell a story in the world of Cyberpunk, but it won't be a one-to-one translation of the game's story." The Cyberpunk movie is being created in partnership with Parmount, now under the Skydance banner after the recent merger . The film will be produced by Lorenzo di Bonaventura, of live-action Transformers fame.

articles.title: It's time to reassess the size of our solar system, scientists say
articles.excerpt: Two leading space scientists say there is a need to redefine the edge of the solar system based on the Milky Way's gravity, including its dark matter.
articles.body: Two leading space scientists say there is a need to redefine the edge of the solar system by presenting a theory which states that measurements of the Milky Way's gravitational field, including its dark matter, redraws the sun's frontier. That theory was put forward by Jim Green, former NASA chief scientist and past director of the space agency's Planetary Science Division, along with Ed Belbruno, a professor of mathematics at Yeshiva University and a senior research associate at Princeton University. The solar system's gravitational frontier extends to nearly 3.8 light-years from the sun , they contend, roughly 241,000 astronomical units (AU), a distance that brings the "edge" of the solar system to within the same scale as the separation between neighboring stars.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the 1st ever green star, a cosmic zombie just in time for Halloween
articles.excerpt: Imagine if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween. Scientists have discovered that our star may go green if it turns into a cosmic zombie after its death in billions of years.
articles.body: How awesome would it be if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween? It turns out that scientists have discovered that our star may indeed go green, but only billions of years from now after its death — and only if it then starts eating planets like a cosmic zombie. That's possible because scientists have discovered that white dwarfs, the type of stellar remnants sun-sized stars leave behind when they die, can actually take on a range of colors including green if they snack on their rocky planets like cosmic cannibals. For stellar scientists, the colors of stars have always been indicative of their temperatures. Cool stars look orange, while stars like the sun look white , and the hottest stars glow pale blue.
